name: Lolabi Kashmiri Wazwan
why_it_matters: Owners Bilal and Nisar run one of the few Sonamarg kitchens that takes wazwan seriously — rista, gushtaba, and rogan josh cooked the long way rather than the convoy-shortcut version. Ranked #3 of 26 restaurants in town on Restaurant Guru, with a 4.7 Google score from regulars who compare it favourably to Srinagar institutions.
insider_tip: A full traditional wazwan tray is pre-order only — call a day ahead. Walk-ins should order the rista with steamed rice; locals call it the meal that decides whether a Sonamarg restaurant is real or for show.
signature_address: 872R+QV5, opposite Main Market, Sonamarg, Ganderbal District, Jammu and Kashmir 191202

name: Dogra Vaishno Bhojnalaya
why_it_matters: The default pure-veg canteen on Sonamarg's Main Bazaar — open since 2001, run by a Dogra family from Jammu. The thali is the workhorse: dal, rajma, two sabzi, rice, roti, pickle. Where Amarnath Yatra pilgrims and Vaishnav travellers eat without thinking.
insider_tip: Their parathas are made fresh to order — aloo and gobhi are the picks, not the menu's harder Punjabi sides. Expect 15 minutes; don't sit down if you're racing the Zoji-La convoy window.
signature_address: Main Bazaar, Sonamarg, Ganderbal District, Jammu and Kashmir 191202

name: Hotel Glacier Heights Restaurant
why_it_matters: One of Sonamarg's longest-running tourist hotels — Indian, Kashmiri, and continental on the same menu, sized for tour-bus dinners and family halts on the Srinagar-Leh run. 4.3 on Restaurant Guru across 1,000+ reviews; ₹1,200-1,500 for two.
insider_tip: Ask for the Kashmiri pulao with mutton yakhni rather than the generic veg thali — it's where the kitchen actually cooks. Reserve the window table on the upper floor for a Thajiwas-side view.
signature_address: Main Bazaar, Sonamarg, Ganderbal District, Jammu and Kashmir 191202

name: Hotel Snowland Sonmarg Restaurant
why_it_matters: 50-room property near the Sonamarg main market with a glass-walled multi-cuisine restaurant — one of the few rooms in town built around the snow view rather than facing it accidentally. Egg biryani is the dish guests reorder.
insider_tip: Non-residents can walk in for lunch when room service isn't blocked; dinner books out fast in peak season (June-September). The kitchen does Kashmiri staples better than the Chinese — order accordingly.
signature_address: Near Main Market, Sonamarg, Ganderbal District, Jammu and Kashmir 191202

name: Paradise Food Court Sonamarg
why_it_matters: The bazaar's volume eatery — a Sonamarg Road dining hall that absorbs tour buses and families on a budget. 4.6 on TripAdvisor (5 reviews) and a regular fixture on Sonamarg restaurant lists; the appetiser counter and quick veg biryani are the reasons it gets repeat traffic.
insider_tip: The Chinese is reliably hot but generic — stick to the biryani and tandoor sides. Service can lag when convoys arrive together; come at 12:30 or 2:30 to skip the squeeze.
signature_address: Sonamarg Road, Sonamarg, Ganderbal District, Jammu and Kashmir 191202

name: JKTDC Hotel Kongposh Restaurant
why_it_matters: The J&K state tourism (JKTDC) canteen attached to Hotel Kongposh — beside the taxi stand on Main Bazaar. Government-run, fixed prices, Indian veg/non-veg standards plus tea and parathas. The default option for budget travellers and Yatra pilgrims who don't want a market negotiation.
insider_tip: Breakfast is the smartest meal here — paratha and egg curry, served in 10 minutes flat. Closed during the Zoji-La winter shutdown (Dec-April) like most of the bazaar; reopens with the road.
signature_address: Small Market, Main Bazaar, near taxi stand, Sonamarg, Ganderbal District, Jammu and Kashmir 191202

name: The Villa Himalaya Restaurant
why_it_matters: Family-run boutique hotel in Kullan village, ~14 km short of Sonamarg on the old Srinagar road, perched on the Sind river. Chef Tapan's kitchen runs the closest thing the valley has to slow-food cooking — trout sourced same-day, kahwa brewed properly, breads baked in-house. Roughly 14 rooms, dining mostly for residents but non-residents accepted with a call ahead.
insider_tip: Trout has to be ordered an hour in advance — they fillet to order, not from a fridge. Bonfire dinners are seasonal; ask when you book. The riverside terrace at lunch is the move, not the dining room.
signature_address: Kullan Village, Old Srinagar-Sonamarg Road, near Gagangir, Ganderbal District, Jammu and Kashmir 191202
